text_blocks.snippet: Texas does not have reciprocity with any other state's bar, meaning lawyers licensed in other states cannot automatically practice law in Texas without meeting specific requirements. However, Texas does allow attorneys to be admitted to the Texas Bar without taking the bar exam if they meet certain criteria, including a minimum Uniform Bar Examination (UBE) score.
No Reciprocity: Texas does not have a reciprocal agreement with any other state that allows for automatic admission to the Texas Bar for attorneys licensed elsewhere.
Admission Without Examination: Texas offers a pathway to admission without taking the bar exam for attorneys who meet specific criteria, including:

list.title: UBE Score:
list.snippet: Applicants can transfer a qualifying UBE score (at least 270) from another jurisdiction.

list.title: Law Degree:
list.snippet: Applicants must hold a J.D. from an ABA-accredited law school or satisfy an exception to the law study requirement.

list.title: Character and Fitness:
list.snippet: The Texas Board of Law Examiners conducts a character and fitness investigation for all applicants.

list.title: Texas Law Component:
list.snippet: Applicants must complete a Texas Law Component.

list.title: MPRE:
list.snippet: Applicants need to document a score of 85 or higher on the Multistate Professional Responsibility Examination (MPRE).

text_blocks.snippet: UBE Adoption: Texas adopted the Uniform Bar Exam (UBE) in 2021. This means that instead of a state-specific exam, Texas now accepts scores from the UBE administered in other jurisdictions.

list.title: Active Practice Not Required:
list.snippet: Beginning in 2020, Texas no longer requires applicants to have actively practiced law for a specific period to be eligible for admission without examination.

list.title: UBE Scores Valid for Five Years:
list.snippet: UBE scores used for transfer to Texas are valid for five years from the date of the exam.

list.title: Character and Fitness:
list.snippet: The Texas Board of Law Examiners handles the character and fitness review, which can take up to nine months.
